A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HDS-QA and HybridDeepSearcher. All 23 pages of v1 and 37 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, prompts, and appendix case studies, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results in Table 2, evidence-retrieval results in Table 3, and additional search-budget analyses and model-output examples in the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and adds controlled experiments, robustness analyses, trajectory statistics, and model-size and summarizer ablations.

M1.justification: The core dataset-generation pipeline, supervised training objective, and reasoning-querying-retrieval procedure remain unchanged. Evidence aggregation was already requested in v1's response-generation prompt. v2 Section 6 adds an optional GRPO training extension using binary correctness rewards from Qwen3-4B-Instruct.

E1.justification: Both versions use Natural Questions-derived HDS-QA and evaluate MuSiQue, FanOutQA, FRAMES, MedBrowseComp, and BrowseComp. Expanding BrowseComp from 50 to 150 questions retains the same o3-solvable-within-five-minutes criterion. The new controls and analyses use retained tasks and domains.

E2.justification: The seven main named baselines are retained; Directly Gen is renamed Naïve Gen. v2 adds an HDS-QA-trained single-query comparator in Table 4. Appendix F adds RAG-R1 to all three case comparisons and removes Search-o1 from the MuSiQue case.

E3.justification: BrowseComp evaluation expands from 50 to 150 questions. FanOutQA gains BLEURT and switches its judging prompt from Zheng et al. to the dataset-specific Zhu et al. prompt. The reported fine-tuning batch size changes from 4 to 32, without establishing that retained results were rerun. New experiments vary backbone, query parallelism, GRPO training, model size, and summarizer configuration.

E4.justification: v2 adds matched-backbone and single-query controls, GRPO experiments, model-size and summarizer ablations, accuracy grouped by evidence requirements, trajectory-diversity statistics, and RAG-R1 failure cases. These substantially expand tests of attribution and robustness. v1 Figure 5's evidence-coverage-versus-turn analysis is removed; its turn, call, and token-budget analyses are retained elsewhere.

E5.justification: Both versions report four trajectory-generation attempts per HDS-QA question with the same success counts. v2's pass@4 uses those existing outcomes. Neither version reports benchmark evaluation seeds, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: BrowseComp results are replaced for the larger sample: HybridDeepSearcher reports 17.2 F1 and 16.0 judged accuracy in v1 versus 15.1 and 13.3 in v2. FanOutQA judged accuracy changes from 25.1 to 20.0 under the revised prompt, while F1 remains 44.1. These replacements use changed conditions. v2 additionally reports BLEURT, controlled-variant results, robustness curves, and trajectory statistics; Table 3's evidence-coverage values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the evidence-coverage numerator from |Ui| to |Ui ∩ Di|, aligning the formula with the already stated intersection of retrieved and gold evidence. This fixes a mathematical definition without establishing a changed retrieval procedure. The added AUC equation formalizes an existing metric; neither version supplies theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims of improved accuracy, efficiency, and search scaling through HDS-QA-supervised hybrid search remain. v2 adds an explicit first-dataset claim concerning more than two parallel subqueries integrated into sequential reasoning, and makes robustness to increasing evidence requirements a headline contribution.

C2.justification: v2 develops a synthesis-bottleneck explanation for baseline failures and interprets the new controls as evidence for hybrid search behavior. It newly discusses fixed question templates, successful trajectories containing incorrect intermediate steps, and reduced dependence on large teachers or summarizers. Section 6 adds a substantive accuracy-efficiency tradeoff: GRPO increases search depth and generally lowers AUC despite higher final accuracy.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies the question-generation model, discloses a 95/5 training-validation split, and explains how excess parallel queries are truncated to the remaining call budget. Appendix A adds GRPO hardware and training settings, and the title page adds a project-page link. Most existing implementation details and generation prompts are retained; downloadable resource availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially revises positioning around decomposition and synthesis, adding discussion of GenDec, Plan*RAG, ReDel, ADaPT, and synthetic web-agent data. v1's discussion of APR, Multiverse, and adaptive parallel-reasoning termination is removed. The revised account distinguishes HDS-QA through broad parallel retrieval followed by evidence synthesis for sequential reasoning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion are substantially rewritten around search scaling and structured aggregation. v2 introduces a separate Discussion section and organizes the appendices into sections A–F. The title and affiliation header also change, while much of the method description and the generation prompts remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column to a single-column layout, with extensively reformatted tables and plots. v1's motivation diagram and evidence-coverage-versus-turn plot are removed; v2 adds robustness and ablation displays. The appendix budget plots are merged, and retained case-study continuations receive individual table captions rather than representing entirely new cases.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the central contribution through the matched-backbone comparison and single-query control in Tables 2 and 4, addressing attribution gaps in v1. Model-size and summarizer ablations further test important dependencies. These gains outweigh the removed coverage-versus-turn analysis and new reporting inconsistencies, including conflicting BrowseComp baseline accuracies between Tables 2 and 8 and summarizer average-drop claims that do not match the displayed rows.
